title: Bias-Preserving Gates and Quantum Error Correction With Dual-Rail Cat Codes
authors: Debjyoti Biswas, Nikhil Sharma, Alberto Salvador, Rui Wang, Mats Granath, Adithi Udupa, Giulia Ferrini
abstract: Scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation requires quantum error-correcting codes that simultaneously support universal logical operations, suppress hardware-specific noise, and enable efficient handling of photon-loss errors. Bosonic encodings such as the dual-rail and cat codes each offer attractive features but also exhibit important limitations when used in isolation. The dual-rail code enables efficient single-photon-loss detection by converting leakage out of the computational subspace induced by photon-loss errors into an erasure error. In contrast, the cat code provides a resource-efficient, bias-tailored error-correction scheme with bias-preserving logical gate operations. Here, we introduce the dual-rail cat code (DRCC), a concatenated bosonic encoding that combines an inner cat code with an outer dual-rail structure, thereby inheriting and enhancing the advantages of both constituent codes. We analyse the error-correction properties of the DRCC and propose a deterministic single-photon-loss correction protocol by concatenating it with an outer repetition code. Exploiting the code's intrinsic noise bias, we construct a universal set of logical gates using only beam-splitter interactions and demonstrate that all logical operations preserve the erasure-biased noise structure. The DRCC offers several distinctive advantages, including the absence of relative geometric phases during gate operations, deterministic erasure detection and correction, and simultaneous syndrome extraction without interrupting stabilisation. These features make the DRCC a promising bosonic code for hardware-efficient, bias-preserving, and erasure-resilient fault-tolerant quantum computation.
summary: The paper introduces and rigorously analyzes the Dual-Rail Cat Code (DRCC), a novel concatenated bosonic code designed for fault-tolerant quantum computing. It demonstrates that DRCC inherits advantages from both dual-rail and cat codes to achieve bias-preserving logical gates and deterministic correction against photon loss. The methodology involves advanced techniques in open quantum systems, making it a significant theoretical contribution to photonic quantum information.
main_problem: Developing fault-tolerant quantum computation protocols that can simultaneously support universal logical operations, suppress hardware noise, and efficiently handle photon-loss errors.
main_result: The proposed Dual-Rail Cat Code (DRCC) offers a highly promising bosonic encoding for FTQC due to its deterministic erasure detection, absence of relative geometric phases during gates, and inherent bias preservation.
method: The authors analyze the error-correction properties using the Knill–Laflamme condition and construct logical gates by projecting engineered Hamiltonians onto the code subspace via continuous dissipation.
model_or_system: The system utilizes bosonic encodings, specifically the concatenated Dual-Rail Cat Code (DRCC), which combines an inner cat code with an outer dual-rail structure. The analysis involves modeling photon loss and dephasing noise using Lindblad master equations.
key_observables: Logical error rates ($\hat{X}, \hat{Z}$ errors), relative geometric phases, success probability of correction protocols, and the satisfaction of the Knill–Laflamme condition.
important_parameters: Photon loss strength ($\kappa$), dephasing strength ($\gamma$), cat state amplitude parameter ($\alpha$), and the order of concatenation (e.g., two-qubit or three-qubit repetition code).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on approximations such as the small-$\alpha$ limit for certain error detection capabilities, and assumes specific dissipation mechanisms can stabilize the desired code manifold.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Wigner functions of cat states, comparisons between different noise models, and schematics detailing multi-step Quantum Error Correction (QEC) protocols using joint parity checks.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the DRCC structure, analyzes its error correction under various noise channels (photon loss/dephasing), details the construction of universal logical gates via engineered dissipation, and finally proposes concatenated QEC protocols to achieve high-order fault tolerance.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant for AMO physicists working on cavity QED or quantum optics because it provides a detailed theoretical framework for implementing robust quantum computation using bosonic modes (photons/cavity fields) as the physical substrate, directly addressing noise mitigation in superconducting or optical setups.

FIG. 2: For DRCC-1 (upper panel), any single-photon loss or gain, as well as arbitrary higher-order photon-loss errors ˆam i or photon-gain errors ˆa†m i on a single mode (m ≥2), either map the logical states to the even-parity leakage subspace or leave them within the odd-parity code space. For the conventional dual-rail code (lower panel), while single-photon loss or gain on either mode map the logical states to the even-parity leakage states {|00⟩, |11⟩, |02⟩, |20⟩} (detectable as erasures), higher-order photon gain processes ˆa†m i (m ≥2) can also populate other odd-parity states, such as {|12⟩, |21⟩}, leading to false-positive syndrome outcomes [20].
